existingRuntimeRequirements: baum-os src/context WorkingContext compositionManifest shape (checkpointId, compressedThroughSequence, tailFromSequence, rehydratedRefs) as the adapted context engine input — mechanics stay in baum-os via the ContextEnginePort
externalSpecRequirements: Master spec (external, non-normative input) §4.3 manifest observability fields: source_type, provenance, priority, freshness, trust_level, token_estimate, inclusion_reason, omitted_sources, compression_applied
ownerDisposition: OQ-1: shared-core owns the port and manifest contract; baum-os owns context mechanics
OQ-4: no trust tiers — trust is an opaque policy decision record (policy_ref/subject_ref/decision)
OQ-5: no trusted-context resolution here; resolver_ref stays a generic opaque reference (the domain resolver authority owns resolution behind its own port)
newInference: Sum of section token_estimates must not exceed token_budget (admission arithmetic, checked by validator)

title: CLG ContextManifest (+ ContextEnginePort surface)
description: Observability contract for why the model saw what it saw. The ContextEnginePort consumer knows only this contract; the concrete context engine (baum-os src/context) remains the implementation. A source being relevant never implies instruction authority: trust decisions are opaque records. The generic runtime must not resolve tenancy facts, principal access, or domain trust.

engine_ref.description: Opaque reference to the concrete context engine implementation behind the port.

resolver_ref.description: Opaque reference to the resolver that produced this section (e.g. a domain resolver behind ContextProviderPort). Generic runtime derives no authority from it.
